title: Membrane WFI: RO, EDI and ultrafiltration | Aquemi
meta: Water for Injection by RO, EDI and ultrafiltration, as Ph. Eur. 0169 allows since 2017: < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin, a written control strategy, ambient.
eyebrow: WATER FOR INJECTION · MEMBRANE · PH. EUR. 0169 · USP · EU GMP ANNEX 1
headline: Water for Injection by membrane, with the control strategy and validation package your inspector will ask for
lead: Our double-pass reverse osmosis (RO), electrodeionization (EDI) and ultrafiltration (UF) skids make Water for Injection (WFI) at ambient temperature, within the USP <85> bacterial endotoxin limit of < 0.25 EU/mL and the USP <645> conductivity limit of 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C, with no plant steam for generation. We design the biofilm and endotoxin controls the EMA expects from a non-distillation system into the skid, and tell you plainly when distillation is the better route.
primary_cta_intent: Route assessment: which systems, which WFI route

blocks.h: The limits are the same as distilled WFI. The evidence you owe is not.
body: USP defines WFI as water purified by distillation or by a process equivalent or superior to distillation in removing chemicals and microorganisms. Since 1 April 2017, Ph. Eur. 0169 also accepts a purification process equivalent to distillation: reverse osmosis, single-pass or double-pass, coupled with other appropriate techniques such as EDI, ultrafiltration or nanofiltration. EU GMP Annex 1 (2022), adopted by Health Canada as GUI-0119, repeats that wording in paragraph 6.10.

Conductivity, Total Organic Carbon (TOC), endotoxin and microbial limits do not change with the route. What changes is the burden of proof. A still removes endotoxin by phase change at high temperature. A membrane system runs at ambient temperature, which the EMA's 2017 questions and answers on non-distillation WFI (EMA/INS/GMP/443117/2017) call an ideal environment for biofilm. So the EMA expects a documented control strategy, developed alongside the design, that shows how the system prevents, detects and removes microbial growth and endotoxin.

Ph. Eur. 0169 also asks that notice is given to the manufacturer's GMP supervisory authority before a membrane WFI system is implemented. USP has no such step. We build the system and the evidence together, so the control strategy, the qualification plan and the notice your regulatory team files draw on the same documents.

blocks.h: How water moves through the skid
blocks.caption: Pretreatment delivers feed that is softened and free of chlorine and chloramine, checked by an oxidant sensor before the first RO pass. Two RO passes in series remove dissolved ions, organics, bacteria and endotoxin. Carbon dioxide passes RO as a gas, so we convert or strip it between the passes before it loads the EDI. EDI polishes conductivity with no regeneration chemicals. The final UF membrane is the last barrier to endotoxin and bacteria. Water below the conductivity and TOC setpoints goes to storage; anything else recirculates or diverts until it recovers. The whole train is hot water sanitized on a schedule set from your data.

blocks.h: From route decision to qualified WFI

items.d: We read your WFI demand, feed water analyses, utility costs, storage temperature and the pharmacopoeias and markets you release into, then recommend membrane or distillation in writing, with the reasons.

Risks, design controls, sanitization, monitoring and maintenance written into a control strategy input and a functional specification you approve. These are the documents your notice to the authority draws on.
Piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) and general arrangement drawings issued for your review. Product-contact welds logged, inspected and traceable to material heat numbers.
The skid runs in our test bay against a protocol you approve: sequences, alarms, oxidant and divert interlocks, a full hot water sanitization cycle, UF integrity test and outlet quality.
After tie-in we repeat the critical tests on your feed water, then execute installation and operational qualification (IQ and OQ).

An initial phase with daily sampling at every point, then a year of data to capture seasonal feed changes, as the EMA questions and answers describe. We write the sampling plan with your validation team and support the sampling.

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Without published plant case studies, how do you show the skid controls microbes and endotoxin?
items.a: With the control strategy on this page, risk by risk, and the evidence behind each line: online total organic carbon (TOC) and conductivity, [ultrafiltration integrity test method and frequency], sanitization proven by temperature at the coldest point, and endotoxin results from FAT and SAT sampling. You review the protocols before FAT, and the sample turnover package shows the format.

items.q: Will you support us during the regulatory notification and inspections?
items.a: We supply the design basis, the control strategy and the qualification data your notification and inspection file need. [Confirm: whether Aquemi engineers attend inspections or answer inspector questions, and on what terms.]

items.q: Will Health Canada and the FDA accept membrane WFI?
items.a: Both inspect against the pharmacopoeia you release to, and USP has allowed WFI by any process equivalent or superior to distillation for many years. Health Canada recognizes USP and Ph. Eur. as Schedule B publications, and its GUI-0119 adopts Annex 1, which names RO coupled with EDI, UF or nanofiltration. Acceptance rests on your data: a sound design, a documented control strategy and a PQ that covers seasonal feed changes.

items.q: Who do we notify, and when?
items.a: Ph. Eur. 0169 asks that notice is given to the manufacturer's GMP supervisory authority before implementation. The EMA questions and answers say that for a site outside the EU it is the authority of the EU importer's Member State, or, where a mutual recognition agreement covers the product, the site's own authority. Your regulatory team confirms which applies to your products and files the notice; we supply the design and control strategy documents behind it.

items.q: Is membrane WFI as safe on endotoxin as a still?
items.a: It can meet the same limit, by a different mechanism. A still relies on one phase change; a membrane system relies on several barriers in series and on keeping them intact and clean. That is why we trend rejection and differential pressure, integrity test the UF, and sample endotoxin after the UF throughout PQ. If your feed carries a high or variable endotoxin load, we say so and model distillation too.

Longer than many teams plan for. The EMA questions and answers describe daily sampling at all points in the initial phase, then performance shown over an extended period, typically a year. Most plants start using the water once the initial phase is complete, on a decision their quality unit documents. Build that year into the project schedule from the start.

items.q: Can we store membrane WFI hot?
items.a: Yes. Annex 1 gives circulation above 70 °C as an example of storage that minimizes microbial growth, not a requirement. Heating ambient WFI to fill a hot loop gives back much of the energy saving, so most membrane WFI plants use an ozonated or regularly sanitized ambient loop instead. Storage and distribution covers both.

items.q: How much energy will we save?
items.a: It depends on your steam cost, power cost, demand profile and storage temperature, so we calculate it for your plant rather than quote a percentage. The route assessment shows energy, water to drain, consumables and membrane replacement per cubic metre of WFI for both routes. [Add Aquemi design figures per cubic metre once validated on a delivered system.]

items.q: Can our corporate standard or export markets rule membrane WFI out?
items.a: They can. Some corporate water standards and some national pharmacopoeias still call for distillation. Check every market you release product into before you choose the route. We include that check in the route assessment.
